With this new implementation, the GitHub issue can finally be closed. Phew. Another thing that I've added has been support for per material attributes, [music] like density, friction, and restitution. In previous versions of my engine, of course, stuff like friction existed, but there was just one global [music] coefficient of friction for the entire world. And now, it can be on a per voxel basis. So, a steel voxel can be heavier than a feather voxel, for example. Now, the weight of objects isn't super obvious. I think right now, you can sort of feel it as you drag various objects about in the world. But, where varying density will really shine, I [...] them cancel out correctly. And then [music] when we remove the object on the left, we can see the principle of torque in action, causing the beam to tilt. A more rigorous test that [music] physics developers like to do is to see how many boxes they can stack. And so, in this scene, I have boxes which are just over half a meter um in terms of scale. And I found that I'm able to stack about six boxes. Once I add seven, the tower starts to wobble a little bit. But, that seems like plenty to me. It's even possible to make a large pile of various shapes, and everything stays together. Nothing explodes. This was actually an issue that I had in my previous engine. Shout-outs to this user called Delayeth on GitHub, but we had quite a long conversation about how if you piled up these objects in a [...] of my friend Kelvin. Voxel objects can now break apart and be edited just like the main grid. The engine is better unit tested, and so much more. I'm now looking for ways to be more serious about this project and more [music] serious about the YouTube channel. So, if you enjoyed this video and want to see more content, more [music] frequent content especially, please leave a like and subscribe. Also, leave a comment.
